scope.flow: Merkl campaign override (overrideCampaign) start/end timestamp constraint checks
evidence: Merkl allows creators to override campaign parameters, with some limitations: creators cannot change the start timestamp of the campaign if it already started, and they cannot set the end timestamp to a time in the past.

But when checking these constraints, the function `overrideCampaign` uses the initial campaign(`_campaign` which comes from `_campaignLookup[_campaignId]`) as a reference point for the start time, instead of the most recent compaign(`campaignOverrides[_campaignId]`).

So in the case in which a creator postpones a campaign, and then, for whatever reason, they decide to postpone it again, they are not allowed to do so if they do it after what was the initial start timestamp.
1. creator sets up a campaign with start time x
creator overrides the campaign and sets its start time to y
creator tries to override the campaign at a time after x but before y, but can't, even though they should
2. creator sets up a campaign with start time x
creator overrides the campaign and sets its start time to y
creator tries to override the campaign and set its duration to a time that if added to y is in the future, but added to x is in the past, but can't, even though they should

ambiguities: Report does not state who may call overrideCampaign or any authorization condition; no unauthorized-caller precondition asserted.
The override attempts are described as failing ('can't, even though they should'); the revert/failure outcome belongs to the separate Impact inventory, so no action step is claimed here.
No explicit numeric values for x, y, or current time are given; only relative ordering (after x, before y) is supported.
The statement that a creator postponing a campaign again is not allowed to do so after the initial start timestamp describes a restriction/mechanism rather than a distinct harmful outcome.
